    Specialization of geometric determinants to finite ground matrices #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.exists_unit_tensor_evaluation (k : Type u_1) {F : Type u_2} [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k F] [Infinite F] {ι : Type u_3} [Finite ι] (p : MvPolynomial ι F) (hp : p ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (E : IntermediateField k F) (_ : Module.Finite k ↥E) (c : ι → ↥E), IsUnit ((MvPolynomial.aeval fun (i : ι) => 1 ⊗ₜ[k] c i) p)

    A geometric polynomial can be made a unit by substituting elements from a finite ground extension into the second factor of its scalar extension. The ground multiple has invertible value already in the second factor.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.exists_ground_invertible_block (k : Type u_1) {F : Type u_2} [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k F] [Infinite F] {a : Type u_3} {n : Type u_4} [Fintype a] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (D : a → Matrix n n F) {t : ℕ} (ht : 0 < t) (z : Fin t × a × Fin t → F) (hz : (blockFamily D z).det ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (_ : 0 < m) (x : Fin m × a × Fin m → k), (blockFamily D fun (j : Fin m × a × Fin m) => (algebraMap k F) (x j)).det ≠ 0

    An invertible geometric block matrix can be replaced by a larger block matrix whose coefficients are in the ground field. The entries of the matrix family itself may be geometric.
